summary: They will not seat you: {the body} votes not to seat you over {the challenge}.
realLife: One life: In 1966 the Georgia House kept him out over his statements against the Vietnam War. The Supreme Court ruled unanimously that a legislator's views cannot disqualify him, and he was seated. Another: In 1880 the California Senate voted to disqualify him after it came out that he had never completed his citizenship. Another: A New York congressman objected to seating Mississippi's members over the denial of Black voters' rights. The House seated them after a vote.
gates: A challenge to your seat on record.
